question_text: Explain the scope and significance of numerical taxonomy.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Scope: how it works
lines: Numerical taxonomy is carried out using
Every observable character is given a number
and a code. Hundreds of characters can be
handled at one time, and each character is given
steps.why: Equal weight and the large number of characters are the two working rules of the method, so they carry the scope mark.
common_mistakes: Writing only that it "uses numbers". Say what is numbered and that weight is equal.
Saying only some characters are chosen. All observable characters are used.
steps.memory_tip: Number the characters, code them, weigh them all the same, let the computer count.
steps.margin_note: Two to three lines. Equal weight is the phrase examiners look for.

steps.label: Significance
lines: Because no character is favoured over another,
the grouping does not depend on one
taxonomist’s opinion. Large data sets can be
compared quickly, and the work can be repeated.
steps.why: The value of the method is that it removes personal judgement from grouping and can be repeated by anyone.
common_mistakes: Saying it proves evolutionary descent. It measures likeness, not ancestry.
Giving no use at all. The question asks for significance.
steps.memory_tip: Equal weight means no favourite character, so no personal opinion in the result.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line plus one reason is the full mark.

insider_note: The book answers this in a single line. Write the equal-weight point as well; it is the part that shows you know the method.
